# Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric

This page describes how to enable Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric and deploy its components: the AI Inference Gateway, the MCP sidecar, and the external credential injection processor.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

To install the Agentic Analytics components for cycle detection, refer to [Configure cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection/configure-cycle-detection).

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Requirements

- A valid Consul Enterprise license configured in your Consul deployment.
- Envoy 1.38.2 or later for the AI Inference Gateway.
- Access to the registry path supplied for your distribution.

External credential injection is not supported on OpenShift.

## Enable the feature gate

Agentic Runtime Fabric features are behind the `consul-ai` [feature gate](/consul/docs/manage/feature-gates), which is disabled by default. Enable it with the following command:

```shell-session
$ consul operator feature set consul-ai enabled
```

On Kubernetes, set `ai.enabled` to `true` to enable the feature gate.

## Pull the component images

Pull the image for each component you deploy. Replace `<registry>` with the registry path supplied for your distribution and `<version>` with a compatible release tag.

| Component | Image |
| --- | --- |
| AI Inference Gateway | `csl-inf-rt` |
| MCP sidecar | `csl-mcp-sc` |
| External credential injection processor | `csl-au-inj` |

For Docker, run the following command for each image:

```shell-session
$ docker pull <registry>/<image>:<version>
```

For Podman, run the following command for each image:

```shell-session
$ podman pull <registry>/<image>:<version>
```

Authenticate to the registry when required and pin an approved release tag or digest in your deployment manifest.

Pulling an image does not configure the component. The AI Inference Gateway still needs model backends, provider credentials, mesh routes, and gateway policy. The MCP sidecar still needs tool service registrations, mesh routes, and tool-access and human-approval policies. Credential injection still needs Vault access, credential bindings, approved routes, and external TLS.

## Deploy on Kubernetes

Set the Helm values for each component you deploy:

| Component | Helm value |
| --- | --- |
| AI Inference Gateway | [`ai.inferenceGateway.image`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-ai-inferencegateway-image) |
| MCP sidecar | [`ai.agent.image`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-ai-agent-image) |
| External credential injection processor | [`terminatingGateways.defaults.credentialInjection.processorImage`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-terminatinggateways-defaults-credentialinjection-processorimage), which has no default |

Consul injects the MCP sidecar into pods annotated with `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role: ai-agent`.

Deploy each image using the configuration supplied with that release.
